text:
Nashville's winning streak reached six games on a night when, by our numbers, it probably shouldn't have. Justus Annunen stopped 27 of 29 shots and saved about 2.4 goals more than the chances against him deserved (goals saved above expected, a measure of how much better a goalie did than the shot quality predicted). He was named the game's first star, and he is the reason Anaheim's five-game winning streak ended at the Honda Center.

The Ducks played the better game. They put up 4.41 expected goals to the Predators' 3.11 (expected goals measures the quality of chances taken), and across 60 shot attempts to 50 they spent more of the night in Nashville's end. Our simulation of every shot gave Anaheim a 69 percent chance to win. Cutter Gauthier fired seven shots on goal and opened the scoring in the first period, then missed a 25 percent look in the third that Annunen turned away. Shane Wright, drafted fourth overall by the Kraken in 2022, scored on a 2 percent chance in the third to make it 3-1, a backhand that reads like a gift from the hockey gods. Jayden Struble and Nils Hoglander had also scored for Nashville, and Steven Stamkos added the last goal with under four minutes left, after Mikael Granlund had cut the lead to one. Laurent Brossoit allowed four goals on a Nashville team that needed only 3.11 expected goals to get them.

The Predators go home with six straight wins, and Roman Josi reached his 800th career point with two assists. Anaheim finishes a five-game run with a loss it can argue it earned the right to avoid, though results are what count. We'd watch whether the Ducks keep controlling games the way they did here.
